solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Upper-class power that's surprising!

parts.note: P is the standard abbreviation for power in physics
Lummy! is an old British exclamation of surprise, so the phrase stands for that cry

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims at how surprising upper-class power can be.
explanation.walkthrough: LUMMY is a dated British cry of astonishment, like 'Gosh!'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plummy voice is the rich, posh accent associated with the British upper classes.

clue.text: Ropes in wandering king one's captured

indicators.note: wandering means moving about aimlessly, so these letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for king, from Latin rex

explanation.surface: A wandering king is caught in ropes and taken captive.
explanation.definitionFit: A captive held in custody; 'one's captured' means one who is captured.

clue.text: At university, clique was annoying

parts.note: up means in residence at a university, especially Oxford or Cambridge
a set is a social clique or circle

explanation.surface: A clique at university proved irritating.
explanation.walkthrough: UP for 'at university' is British usage: one goes up to Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: To have distressed or irritated someone is to have troubled them.

clue.text: What could become calmer I wonder

indicators.note: could become means these letters can be reshaped into another word

explanation.surface: Someone ponders what might make them calmer.
explanation.definitionFit: A marvel or wonderful event that seems beyond natural explanation.

clue.text: Gummy bears finally located by second year

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word bears

parts.note: a tick is a moment, as in 'just a tick'

explanation.surface: A gummy bear candy is found beside a second-year student.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gummy bears' reads as the sweet, but 'Gummy' alone is the definition. TICK for a second is British usage: 'back in a tick'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something coated in glue-like substance that clings to the fingers.

clue.text: Commodity American explorer brought back to company

indicators.note: brought back means turned round, read backwards

parts.note: John Cabot explored the North American coast; Sebastian Cabot also explored the Americas

explanation.surface: An explorer of the Americas brings goods back to his trading company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought back' turns the explorer's name round. 'American explorer' could also suggest Columbus or Lewis, but only Cabot fits the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Tobacco leaf has long been a major traded crop, a product bought and sold in bulk.

clue.text: Soviet official finds person of merit with girl in vehicle

indicators.note: in places the person and the girl inside the vehicle

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour, so a holder of it
a miss is a girl or young woman

explanation.surface: A Soviet official finds a distinguished man and a girl in a car.
explanation.walkthrough: The Order of Merit is a British honour awarded by the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A Communist Party officer responsible for political education in Soviet units, or a head of a government department.

clue.text: You formerly could get a railway annual

parts.note: ye is the old form of you

explanation.surface: In the past you could take a railway's annual pass.
explanation.definitionFit: Happening once every twelve months, like an annual event.

clue.text: Manners shown by cabin staff and driver of plane

parts.note: airs are affected manners, as in 'airs and graces'
the cabin crew are the attendants aboard an aircraft

explanation.surface: Flight attendants display their manners alongside the pilot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'driver of plane' suggests the pilot, but it is the propeller that drives the aircraft forward.
explanation.definitionFit: A propeller is the rotating device that pulls or pushes an aircraft through the sky.

clue.text: One who famously thrived on turning wicket scoring century

definitions.text: One who famously thrived on turning

parts.note: W is the cricket scoring abbreviation for wicket
hitting runs is scoring them in cricket
a ton is a hundred, a century in cricket

explanation.surface: A cricketer thrived on a turning wicket and scored a hundred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning wicket' reads as a spinning cricket pitch. Dick Whittington, of English folklore and pantomime, heard bells telling him to 'turn again' and became Lord Mayor of London.
explanation.definitionFit: The folk hero turned back towards London at the bells' call and prospered, becoming Lord Mayor three times.

clue.text: Complain about Menace initially in Beano comic

indicators.note: comic as an adjective means funny or absurd, signalling the letters are rearranged into a new order
initially points to the opening letter of Menace

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles about Dennis the Menace's first appearance in the Beano comic.
explanation.walkthrough: The Beano is a long-running British children's comic whose star is Dennis the Menace. M goes in BEANO and 'comic' rearranges all six letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To lament or grumble over something is to express sorrow or dissatisfaction about it.

clue.text: Youngster left in bed

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for left inside the word for a bed

parts.note: a cot is a small bed, especially a baby's

explanation.surface: A child has been left lying in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A young male horse, and by extension a young or inexperienced player, as in a colts team.

clue.text: Fur keeps friend out of cold

indicators.note: friend stands outside, wrapped round, the word for cold

parts.note: china is Cockney rhyming slang for mate (china plate)
a chill is a cold, or coldness

explanation.surface: A fur coat keeps a friend from catching cold.
explanation.walkthrough: CHINA for friend comes from Cockney rhyming slang 'china plate' = mate. 'keeps' is a link here.
explanation.definitionFit: A South American rodent whose very soft grey pelt is prized for luxury garments.

clue.text: Organise mate with alternative arrangement in this!

definitions.text: Organise mate with alternative arrangement in this!

indicators.note: an alternative arrangement of the letters means they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice to set up a partner swap within a three-person relationship.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of ORGANISE and MATE together rearrange to the twelve letters; the whole clue then describes the domestic set-up itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase names a household or sexual arrangement involving three people, one partner sharing with another.

clue.text: One keeps dry — beats rain storms

indicators.note: storms means rages violently, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone stays dry while the rain beats down in storms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeps dry' looks like staying out of the rain; here it means refusing alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: A teetotaller avoids alcoholic drinks; 'dry' describes someone who does not drink.

clue.text: Go round space with enchanting woman, about fifty

parts.note: an en is a printing space, half an em

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the enchantress wraps round the fifty letter

parts.note: Circe is the sorceress of Greek myth who enchanted Odysseus' men
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A man circles the room with a bewitching woman of about fifty.
explanation.walkthrough: EN is a printer's unit of space.
explanation.definitionFit: To surround or form a circle about something is to go all the way round it.

clue.text: Reserves extra food with group consuming tons

indicators.note: consuming means eating, so the food and group swallow up the abbreviation for tons

parts.note: seconds are a second helping of food
a ring is a group, as of conspirators

explanation.surface: Some reserved supplies of extra food are kept by a group that eats tons.
explanation.walkthrough: The tons abbreviation is swallowed at the join between the food and the group, not inside either word.
explanation.definitionFit: The second string of a team are its substitutes or reserve players, not the first choice.

clue.text: Neat supervisor cooked chowder

indicators.note: cooked means altered or falsified, as in cooking the books, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A tidy supervisor has made some chowder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' looks like tidy, but is an old word for cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: One who tends cattle; neat is an archaic word for oxen or cows.

clue.text: Play guitar having a time in bed

indicators.note: having means holding within, so the guitar word contains the other pieces

parts.note: to strum is to play a guitar by brushing the strings

explanation.surface: Someone strums a guitar while lying in bed for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bed' suggests sleep, but means a layer of rock.
explanation.definitionFit: A geological layer of rock or sediment, as a seam or bed in the ground.

clue.text: Blunders may secure first in Oxford and Cambridge course

indicators.note: may secure means could hold fast inside, so the blunders word encloses a letter

parts.note: trips are slips or blunders

indicators.note: first in points to the opening letter of Oxford

explanation.surface: Mistakes might win a place on an Oxbridge course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oxford and Cambridge' looks like one unit; Oxford gives only its O.
explanation.definitionFit: The tripos is the honours degree examination and course of study at Cambridge University.

clue.text: Mole takes holiday by lake perhaps

parts.note: a break is a short holiday
a lake is one example of a body of water

explanation.surface: A mole takes a holiday beside a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mole' suggests the burrowing animal or a spy, but here it is a harbour wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A mole is a massive stone pier or barrier protecting a harbour from the sea's waves.

clue.text: Meat upsets carnivore's insides

indicators.note: upsets means overturns, so a stretch of letters is turned round
insides limits the turning to the middle pair of letters

parts.note: a lion is the classic meat-eating big cat

explanation.surface: A piece of meat upsets the stomach of a meat-eater.
explanation.walkthrough: LION's inside letters IO are turned to OI.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut of meat taken from the back of an animal between the ribs and hips.

clue.text: American inhabitant putting up a shopping complex

indicators.note: putting up in a down clue means the letters are read from the bottom upwards, backwards

parts.note: a mall is a shopping centre

explanation.surface: An American resident is putting up a new shopping mall.
explanation.walkthrough: A then MALL, read upward, spells the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The llama is a South American animal of the camel family, living in the Andes.

clue.text: Cleaner finding nasty smell in surface externally

indicators.note: in places the smell word inside the outer letters
externally points to the outside letters of surface, its first and last

parts.note: pong is British slang for a bad smell

explanation.surface: A cleaner discovers a nasty smell on the outside of a worktop.
explanation.walkthrough: PONG goes between S and E, the outer letters of 'surface'.
explanation.definitionFit: A porous pad, natural or synthetic, used for washing and wiping things clean.

clue.text: Pick from menu that choice fowl

indicators.note: pick from means select letters out of the following words

explanation.surface: A diner chooses that choice poultry dish from the menu.
explanation.definitionFit: A small songbird that climbs tree trunks; fowl is used loosely for any bird.

clue.text: Take great steps to travel in pursuit of saint

indicators.note: in pursuit of means following behind, so the travel word comes after the saint

parts.note: to ride is to travel on a horse or vehicle

explanation.surface: Someone strides out to follow a saint on a pilgrimage.
explanation.definitionFit: To walk with long, decisive paces is to move forward with big steps.

clue.text: Run through the limit after one mile

indicators.note: after means the limit word follows the one and mile pieces

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
the pale is a boundary or limit, as in 'beyond the pale'

explanation.surface: A runner goes past the limit after running one mile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run through' reads as an athletics phrase, but means pierce with a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: To pierce someone or something with a spear or sword is to skewer them.
